questions.q: Why do "Texas", "TX", and "texas " cause problems in a grouped report, even though each individual record is accurate?
options: They are treated as three or four unrelated string values instead of one state
Salesforce reports cannot group on text fields at all
Grouped reports require picklist fields to run at all
Trailing spaces cause the report to fail silently
questions.explain: A grouped report, a filter, and an exact matching rule all compare strings literally. Different spellings or casing of the same real value produce separate buckets.

questions.q: What is the most reliable way to prevent inconsistent values in a field with a known, finite set of valid options?
options: Add a validation rule that blocks every misspelling you've seen so far
Convert the field to a picklist so values are selected, not typed
Train every user individually on the correct spelling
Leave it free text but add REGEX to normalize capitalization
questions.explain: A picklist removes the chance to introduce variance in the first place, since the value is selected from a controlled list rather than typed freely.

questions.q: What does enabling State and Country/Territory Picklists change?
options: It deletes all existing address data and requires re-entry
It only affects new orgs, never an org with existing records
It converts State and Country fields across standard addresses to controlled picklists, with a cleanup pass for existing data
It replaces Duplicate Rules for Account and Contact matching
questions.explain: This Setup feature turns free-text State/Country fields into standardized picklists org-wide and includes a one-time cleanup pass for pre-existing free-text values.

questions.q: What does TRIM(text) do in a formula or Flow?
options: Converts text to uppercase
Replaces one substring with another
Deletes the field's value entirely
Removes leading and trailing whitespace from the text
questions.explain: TRIM strips leading and trailing spaces, which is exactly the kind of invisible inconsistency (like "texas " with a trailing space) that breaks exact matching and grouping.

questions.q: Why run cleanup logic like TRIM/UPPER in a before-save Flow instead of relying on users to type carefully?
options: It applies the same cleanup automatically on every save, including Data Loader imports, without depending on any one person remembering
Before-save Flows are the only way to edit a field in Salesforce
Flows run only once per day as a scheduled batch
It prevents the field from ever being edited again after the first save
questions.explain: A before-save Flow runs on every save path — manual entry or bulk import — so the standard holds consistently instead of depending on individual discipline.
